Commentary.Commentary: Now. The bowling. I guess one way of looking at this is Tendai Chisoro - when the opposition's run rate has nearly touched 8, he has gone at less than 6 an over - 0/56 in his 10 overs. The others were pummeled any which ways but did succeed in bowling a couple of decent overs in Powerplay 3. If 67 all out on Wednesday was not demoralizing enough, then don't know what will a target of 400 do today. Join us back at 1330 local (1130 GMT) for the second innings.

A word for Asif Ali as well. He came in, just strut his stuff, smashing 50 from 22 balls but yet went unknown because the focus was mainly on Fakhar's 200 and Pakistan's 400. If the openers added 304 in 252 balls, Zaman and Asif added an unbeaten 95 in just 48 balls for the second wicket.

Spectacular batting cannot be said from Pakistan but when both openers get to triple figures, we cannot avoid that term. This is just the 7TH INSTANCE of a Pakistani opening pair scoring tons in ODI cricket, with the last instance being that of Mohammad Hafeez and Nasir Jamshed against India in Dhaka, in 2012. They were given a few chances and well, they made the most use of it. Interestingly, Zaman was on 0 when Imam was on 18, yet overtook him and played all the 50 overs.

A day for milestones. First the Pakistan openers putting on the first ever triple century opening stand in ODIs. Then Fakhar Zaman going on to register the first double ton by a Pakistan batsman. The tourists would have registered their first ever score of 400 as well but fell short - thanks to a wonderful death bowling effort from Donald Tiripano.

PAKISTAN DO NOT REACH 400! A moral victory for the fielding side. Another wonderful delivery, a yorker, on middle, Zaman can only dig it out towards the bowler. But a misfield results in a single and the Asian side finishes on 399/1!
A yorker now, dug out to long off for a run. That is a 22-BALL 50 FOR ASIF, something to take note for the future...

SIX! SLAM! On next to no time, this guy has come and with the spotlight on Fakhar Zaman reaching his double ton, smashed a run short of 50 in just 21 balls. A bad ball of course, a high full toss, Asif swings it into oblivion over mid-wicket!
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for one.
Full and outside off, another yorker-type delivery, pushed towards long off for a run.

A good start to the over. Very full outside off, driven towards cover. There is a good throw to the bowler who disturbs the stumps and it is referred upstairs - but replays confirm that Zaman is in. A single taken.
Who will bowl the last over? Can he restrict Pakistan to 399 or less? Donald Tiripano will be the brave guy...

FOUR! Excellent, simply excellent. Tell you why. The ball is not a bad one at all - a very full ball, almost a yorker, but Asif calmly gets across, comes a touch forward, then takes it on the full and eventually paddles it between short fine lag and backward square leg for a boundary! THIS IS NOW PAKISTAN'S HIGHEST ODI TOTAL - bettering their 385/7 against Bangladesh in Dambulla in 2010.
A full toss, bunted down to long on for a run.
Full and outside off, almost a yorker, digs it out towards cover for a single.
FOUR! Tremendous batting. Gets across and paddles it over short fine leg for a boundary!
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, driven wide of long off for a couple.
The batsman goes after this one but misses the line completely.

SIX! Unbelievable shot! Tell you, this guy... ohh... absolutely lovely to see charismatic batting in a bash-bash bang-bang game. Full and outside off, Ali backs away a touch and simply carves it over cover!
A yorker outside off, Ali looks to dig it out but misses.
WIDE. Miles outside off, left alone.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! When it goes bad for you, it keeps going bad for you. A slower ball outside off, Asif is early into his slog and gets a top edge which goes high in the air. But such is his luck that three men converge - mid-wicket, cover and long off - yet the ball lands in between! Two runs taken. A nice lesson to all those studying geometry - how to trisect angles.

FOUR! BEAUTY! Very nicely done. A full toss outside off, Asif gets across and just gives direction to the ball to reach the fence. Makes a paddle and directs it to the fine leg fence - perfectly bisecting short fine leg and backward square leg. Just get the feeling that Pakistan have discovered a wonderful talent in Asif Ali - in terms of technique and power.
Full and around off, pushed down to long off for a single.
WIDE. Full and well outside off, Zaman lets it go.
Full and around off, pushed down to long on for a run.

FOUR! MAIDEN DOUBLE HUNDRED FOR ZAMAN! He has finally done it. After 16 ODI innings, he has finally managed to reach that landmark. Full and wide outside off, Zaman does not go leg side this time - rather stays put and lofts it over cover for a boundary. Takes his helmet off, does the sajda and then embraces his partner. The Pakistan dressing room is all smiles. Finally, after 21 years, Saeed Anwar's long-standing record of 194 is broken. He achieved that feat against India in 1997.
A yorker on middle, dug out back to the bowler.
What a lovely shot this is. This match has all been about ugly heaves and hence it feels nice if a classical shot is played. Full and outside off, AA carves this beautifully over cover for a single.
A yorker outside off, Ali looks to steer it through the off side but misses.
SIX! PUMMELED! A length ball outside off, Asif swings this as clean as a whistle and clears the sightscreen with ease! 350 UP FOR PAKISTAN! Can they get that elusive 400?
Blessing Muzarabani time. 9-0-63-0 are his figures so far.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single. 10 from that over.
The batsman drives this through the covers. They pick up a single.
Full and wide outside off, Zaman reaches out to drive but misses.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.

FOUR! PLUNDERED! No one in the deep on the leg side and Fakhar takes full toll. Moves to within a hit of reaching that elusive double ton. Walks across his stumps, takes another full toss and smears it over mid-wicket for another boundary. Moves to 196 and this is now the HIGHEST INDIVIDUAL ODI SCORE BY A PAKISTAN BATSMAN.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Oh dear... it goes from bad to worse to worst to I don't know what for Zimbabwe. Full and wide outside off, Zaman reaches out and squeezes it towards point. Two men converge - Chigumbura from sweeper and a fielder from third man - the former gets to the ball first but misses to pick it. The ball hits his left leg and deflects past the backing up fielder to the ropes! Zaman into the 190s now!
Who is in to face the music? Wellington Masakadza has bowled out. One of the 'better' death bowlers for Zimbabwe - Donald Tiripano to bowl.
Full and outside off, biffed wide of long off for a brace. 11 from the over, 44 from the last 4!
Outside off, lofted over cover for a single.
On middle and leg, almost a yorker, Fakhar digs it out back to the bowler. Asif wants a single but is denied.
FOUR! MURDERED! A short ball wide outside off, Zaman crashes it over point and gets successive boundaries.

FOUR! The batsman is well across the stumps and the bowler bowls it well outside leg. Cannot blame him at all. Zaman swings it over short fine leg and gets a boundary. This is now his HIGHEST SCORE IN ALL LIST A CRICKET.
Outside off, played straight to point.
FOUR! Powerful striking. Very full outside off, Asif bludgeons this past the non-striker and beats long on running to his left! 13 from the over, 33 from the last 3!
ANOTHER WIDE. Action replay of the previous delivery.
WIDE. Well outside off, probably anticipating Asif to shuffle across. The batsman doesn't and it is wided.
DOT BALL! Outside off, played straight to cover.
Driven towards the mid off region. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a run.
Comes down the track, takes it on the full and then heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Yet another of those 'how-on-earth-did-that-get-to-the-boundary?' strokes. A full toss outside off, Zaman shapes up to play the reverse sweep, plays it unconvincingly, the ball hits the lower half of the bat but still rolls all the way to the backward point fence.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. 10 from the over, 20 off the last 2!
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, chipped towards long off for a single.
Short and outside off, cut over point. Good tumbling stop by Peter Moor in the deep. Two runs taken.
Outside off, calmly steered to third man for a single.

FOUR! 'That is the way Asif got off the mark in T20Is as well' comments Ramiz Raja on air. Full and wide outside off, Ali throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which flies through the vacant slip cordon to the third man fence.
Asif Ali is the new man in at number 3, replacing Imam.

OUT! In the sky and taken by Tarisai! Wow. Stop the press. Zimbabwe have got a wicket. They have taken a catch. Off the innumerable drag sweeps, finally one has gone to hand. It always was on the cards, only being a matter of when the visiting side picked it. Imam slogged this one high in the air, towards mid-wicket in the deep but could not quite get the distance. Musakanda had to move just slightly to his left and pouched the catch safely. Good sportsmanship from the Zimbabwe fielders as they go across to Imam to congratulate him. What an innings - what a stand. 304/1 are Pakistan.
A full toss outside leg, Fakhar looks to paddle but the ball hits the bottom half of the bat and rolls to square leg. A single taken.

FOUR! Ugly heave-ho. Landed on middle and leg, Zaman drags it wide of the man at square leg in the deep for a boundary to raise the 300-RUN OPENING STAND. This is just the fourth instance of a pair registering a triple hundred stand in ODIs.

FOUR BYES! Interesting decision from Ian Gould. Full and outside leg, Zaman tries to play the reverse sweep, then attempts to paddle but misses. The keeper is blinded behind and the ball races away to the fine leg fence.
Full and down the leg side, swept towards fine leg for a single.
'GREAT! GREAT!' shouts the keeper. A dot ball it is. Gold dust for the home side. A yorker outside leg, Imam can only push it back to the bowler.
Yes! What an excellent over! Just 4 from it. Full ball well outside off, almost a yorker, Zaman gets low to sweep, but misses.
Another full toss, bunted down the ground for just a run again. What an over this has been - can he finish off well?
A low full toss outside off, FZ drags it towards long on for a single.
Similar line, this time he slashes hard but misses.
Smart ploy, as he sees the batsman move across and fires it wide outside off. Fakhar lets it go but it is not wided.
Full and wide outside off, Zaman reaches out and lofts it wide of long off for a couple.

POWERPLAY 3 TIME. 5 fielders allowed outside the circle. Will it make any difference? How much will Pakistan clobber in these final 10? At least a 110 would be on their minds. A score less than that would be a moral victory for the home side.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, Fakhar looks to sweep but misses. The batsmen run through for a single and a leg bye is signalled.

FOUR! IMPERIOUS! That is the record! HIGHEST EVER OPENING STAND IN ODIS! Goes past the record last set by Sanath Jayasuriya and Upul Tharanga in Leeds in 2006, against England. Gets to the milestone in style, getting low and swiping it wide of the man at deep mid-wicket.
A rarity. A dot ball. Pitched outside leg, Zaman looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
The batsman is already way outside the leg stump and the bowler follows him, firing it well outside the pitch. Imam dances out and flicks it towards short fine leg for a single.
Wellington Masakadza to bowl now.
SIX! 17 from the over! This is carnage! A slower ball on middle, Zaman swings it over the square leg fence for his 5th maximum. He moves onto 156.
Way too wide this time outside off, the umpire signals a wide.
Good bowling! Knowing that Zaman is targeting the leg side. Blessing bowls it wide outside off. FZ swings but misses.
Slower bumper on off, Imam pulls it through to deep square leg for a run.
FOUR! Second in the over! Full and outside off, Imam squeezes it through point and the ball races away.
Slower ball outside off, Imam swings but misses.
Full and wide outside off, the batsman lets it be. Wide signaled.
FOUR! He is now seeing the ball like a football! This is short and on the body, Imam pulls it over the mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

TOP EDGE AND SIX! 150 now up for Zaman. 200 is certainly on the cards. He gets to that milestone in style! A full toss on the pads. Zaman goes for the sweep but the ball takes the top edge and goes over the fine leg fence for a biggie. This is now Pakistan's best partnership in ODIs for any wicket.
The batsman tried to sweep that one but missed it and was hit on the pads.
FOUR! This time he finds the fence at mid-wicket! Once again goes for the heave and hits it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.

There it is, 100 for Imam. His second in the series. Another excellent knock by the youngster. His 100 percent conversion rate remains intact. He works this around the corner for a run to get to that milestone. Also the 250 is up for Pakistan. How many more will they get?
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and wide outside off, Zaman hits it down to long off for a run.
FOUR! Bludgeoned! Full and wide outside off, once again it is right in the arc of Zaman. He cracks it through covers for a boundary.
Full on off, Imam this time hits it closer to the man at covers for only a run.
Fuller in length on off, Imam strokes it through covers and calls two and gets two.
Full and wide outside off, the batsman hits it to point.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Flatter on off, punched to covers.
Streaky runs! Uses his feet and tries to swing but gets an outside edge through short third man for a couple.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
Worked with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
SIX! There is no stopping this guy today! Clears the front leg, gets the ball right in his zone. Full and on middle. Zaman smashes it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Shorter in length on middle, Imam pulls it down to deep square leg for a single.
Full and wide outside off, Imam squeezes it to point.
Donald Tiripano is back on.
Drinks!
Uses his feet and makes it into a low full toss but finds mid-wicket.
They now surpass the record courtesy an extra. Down the leg side, Zaman misses the paddle sweep and the umpire signals it a wide.
Clips it through square leg and the batsmen take a run. The two now equal the highest ever opening stand for Pakistan.
On the shorter side, Zaman pulls it towards mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A dot! That should have been put away! Short and down the leg side. Imam pulls it hard but straight to the fielder at short fine leg.
Slower through the air on middle, Imam tucks it around the corner and some good running by the batsmen sees them take two. He is into the 90s now.
A brace to end the over! Another short ball on the body. Zaman pulls it towards short fine leg. The fielder misfields and the batsmen run two. 15 from the over, not a good return for Muzarabani.

FOUR! BRUTE! Do not put your hand to stop that one! That has been hit like a rocket. Short and on middle, Zaman pulls it through mid-wicket. It races to the fence like a tracer bullet. Three consecutive boundaries.
FOUR! Excellent placement! Short and outside off, Zaman shows finesse. He guides it through backward point and fetches himself another boundary.
EDGE BUT FOUR! Riding his luck now is Fakhar Zaman! He swings, targeting the mid-wicket area. The ball though takes the top edge. Goes over the keeper and into the fence.
Full outside off, Zaman tries to drag it through mid-wicket but finds the fielder.
Good length on off, Imam guides it towards point for a run.
Blessing Muzarabani is back into the attack.
SIX! BANG! Ends the over in style! Gets to the pitch of the delivery and tonks it over the long on fence for a maximum.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.

FOUR! 100 for Zaman, he brings it up in style! His second in the series. Almost a similar delivery with which he got to his fifty. Short and outside off, Zaman goes back and cuts it through point and the ball races away. Takes his helmet off and shows his bat to the crowd. Still a lot of time to go, can he score a double ton? You can't rule it out. Also the 200-run stand comes up between the two openers.
Uses his feet and tucks it on the leg side to move onto a number which the Australians believe to be unlucky for them, 87.
Working his way to his 100 is Zaman. 97 he moves onto. He tucks it around the corner for a run.
Plays the paddle sweep towards fine leg. Imam completes one and wants a second but is rightly sent back by his partner.
Wellington Masakadza is back on.
Flatter on middle, Zaman punches it to mid-wicket.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Short and on the body, Imam pulls it towards deep square leg for a run.
Uses his feet and takes it on the full. Hits it hard towards the bowler who does not stop it and a run is taken.
Tosses it up outside off, Zaman hits it to covers.
On the pads, Imam flicks it through square leg for a run.
Fullish on off, Zaman pushes it to covers.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
FOUR! This will add salt to the wound! Full and outside off, Imam times it through covers an the ball races through to the fence.

In the air... it should be the first wicket for Zimbabwe but the fielder at long off has made a complete meal of it. A full ball on off, Imam chips it towards long off. Elton Chigumbura there runs in, slides and tries to take it but the ball brushes his fingers and drops onto the ground. The batsmen take two. That should have been taken and the hosts needed that. Hamilton is not a happy man and rightly so.
5 away now! On the shorter side, Zaman punches it down to long off for a run.
FOUR! Not the right delivery to bowl with the field up on the off side. Full and outside off, Zaman flays it through cover-point for another boundary. Zaman now is a big hit away.
Slower through the air on leg stump, Imam makes room and guides it to short third man.
Quicker and fuller on middle, Zaman eases it down to long off for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. He moves onto 89.
Fires this just outside off, Zaman tries to guide it through short third man but misses.
Dances down the track and strokes it towards the bowler. He does not stop it and a single results.
Comes around the wicket and lands it outside off, Zaman drives it square on the off side for a couple. 10 from this over also.

SIX! First in this innings! The change of bat has done the trick. Brilliant pick up shot! On a length around middle, Zaman goes down on one knee and picks it over the square leg fence for a biggie. Only the 4th maximum of this series for Pakistan, maybe this is one area where they can work on. Interestingly, the current ODI average of both the batsmen now reads 65.8.
On the pads, Zaman tucks it to mid-wicket.
Fuller in length on off, Imam strokes it down to long off for a single.
Slower ball on the stumps, Zaman pushes it down to long on for a run. He moves onto 80.
On a length around off, Zaman goes for the slog sweep but gets an inside edge towards short fine leg.
Shorter in length on middle, Zaman pulls it hard down to long on for a run.
Fires it outside off, Zaman goes for the cut but is beaten by the extra bounce.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Imam tries the sweep but misses.

In the air... but safe! So luck also favoring Pakistan. Zaman is nimble on his feet and tries to go big. He only manages to slice it towards long on. The fielder comes running in but can't get to the ball. A single taken.
Steps down the track and makes it into a full toss. Zaman hits it down towards long on. It is a touch wide of the fielder which enables the batsmen to run two.
Makes room and Chisoro follows him. Imam tucks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Tendai Chisoro is back on.
So just 7 from the over despite going for a boundary! Fuller in length on off, Imam strokes it through mid off for a run.
Goes fuller outside off, Imam goes for the booming drive but does not connect.
FOUR! The fourth ball is a poor one! On the shorter side outside off, Imam waits for it and cuts it through point. The ball races away.
Back of a length on off, Zaman punches it towards covers for a run. Good three balls to begin with.
On the shorter side, Imam pulls it through mid-wicket. There is a fielder in the deep so just a single results.
Slower delivery on middle, Imam tries to flick but closes the face of the bat a little too early. He gets a soft leading edge to mid-wicket.
Hamilton Masakadza is into the attack. The captain has now taken matters into his own hands.
A single to end the over! 13 from it. Imam flicks it to deep square leg and keeps strike.
On the shorter side. Imam picks the length up early and pulls it hard towards mid-wicket. The fielder there makes a good stop.
Very full on middle, Imam drives it down to long on. He calls for two and gets two.
FOUR! 10 from the first three now! Poor bowling, bowls it short and outside off. Bread and butter for Imam. He cuts it through point and gets his 4th boundary.
Short and on middle, Imam pulls it through mid-wicket and takes two. 6 from the first two balls.
FOUR! Up and over! Imam uses his feet. Makes the ball into a half-volley and then chips it over the mid off fielder for a boundary. He has got to his fifty, is it time to step on the accelerator?
Comes down the track and drives it down to long on and retains stroke.
Flatter on off, Imam defends it.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Another ball down the leg side, Imam misses the sweep this time and it is wided again.
Down the leg side, Imam goes for the pull but misses. The keeper appeals but it was maybe to put the umpire off. It does not make a difference as it is signaled a wide.
Tucks it around the corner for a run.
Driven towards the mid off region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Clips it with the turn through mid-wicket for a run.

Fifty for Imam this time! He had a rare failure in the last match but now is back to doing things which he has been doing throughout this series. He works this off his pads towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end. His first half century in this format to add to his 2 centuries. He has a hundred percent conversion rate. Not good signs for Zimbabwe.
Length around off, Imam defends it.
Fuller in length on the pads, Zaman clips it through square leg. He completes one and wants a second but is sent back by his partner.
On off, Zaman mistimes it towards the bowler.
Outside off, guided down to third man for a run.
The bumper on middle, Imam pulls it through mid-wicket and takes two.
Drives it down to long on for a run.
Short and down the leg side, Imam goes for the pull but misses. Wide called by the umpire but that should have been pulled away for a boundary.
Follows the batsman again and Zaman clips it to deep square leg for a run.
Another ball on the pads, Zaman works it towards short fine leg for a single. The fielder there dives over the ball and concedes an extra run.
On the shorter side, Imam punches it down to long on for a run.
Floated up on off, Imam strokes it back to the bowler.
On the pads, Zaman works it towards fine leg for a single.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Another half-tracker and it comes at a comfortable height for the batsman. He pulls it down towards long on for a couple.
Not learning! He goes short again on middle, Imam has all the time in the world as he pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.

Hit hard again but good fielding! Poor bowling this! Short and outside off again. The batsman goes back and slaps it towards covers. The man there dives to his right and makes a half stop. The batsmen run one.
FOUR! Crunched! Short ball on middle, Zaman flat-bats it through mid on and the ball crosses the fence in no time.
Back of a length on middle, Zaman defends it back to the bowler.
Richard Ngarava is back on.
Darts it on middle, Zaman punches it down to long on for a single.
Works it around the corner for a run.
Dances down the track and swings. The ball goes off the inner half towards deep mid-wicket. The batsmen think about two but settle for a run.
Uppish but safe! Slower through the air. Zaman is a little early into the shot. He chips it towards mid-wicket but it falls well short.
Eases it through mid on for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A single to end the over! Imam flicks it with the turn to square leg for a run. 5 from the over after the drinks break.
Slightly shorter this time on middle, Zaman punches it down to long on for a run.
One again bowls it on the pads, the bowler maybe does not want to give the batsman room to open his arms. Zaman works it to mid-wicket.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
On the pads again, this time he flicks it to the fielder in the deep and only a single results.
On the pads, Imam tucks it through square leg. It is in the gap and the batsmen run two.
Drinks! Once again the openers have provided Pakistan with an excellent start. Zimbabwe need wickets after the break or they will be staring down at a huge target.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total. 11 from this over.
Eases it down to long off for a run.

FOUR! In the air... but through the hands of the fielder! Zaman comes down the track and goes for the heave with the turn. He does connect well but does not get the desired elevation. It goes towards the fielder at deep mid-wicket who runs to his left, stretches his hands up but the ball bursts through for a one-bounce boundary. This also brings up the 100-run stand. Their third in the four games played in this series.

FOUR! Fifty for Zaman, his 6th in this format! He gets a gift to get there. Short and wide outside off, a poor ball with no protection out on the boundary. Zaman goes back and cuts it through cover-point and gets to the milestone. His purple patch continues. He raises his bat to acknowledge the applause from the crowd.
This time he hits it away from the bowler and down to long on for a run.
Steps down the track but the bowler bowls it short. Imam strokes it back to the bowler.
On middle, Zaman works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Darts it on the stumps, Zaman punches it back to the bowler.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On off, cut to point.
Flighted ball on off, Zaman drives it towards mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder from covers runs to his left and makes a half stop but does not concede an extra run.
Quicker outside off, Zaman cuts it to point.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Eases it through mid on and takes a run.
Short again and width is also offered outside off, Imam cuts it through point. The fielder gives it a chase and manages to pull it back just inside the ropes. Three runs taken by the batsmen.
Tosses this up on off, Zaman drives it back to the bowler.
Slightly shorter on middle, FZ punches it down to long on for a run.
Flighted ball on middle, Imam tucks it through square leg for a run.
Wellington Masakadza is introduced into the attack. Spin from both ends now.
Well he maybe wants to get to his fifty with a biggie. Uses his feet again and has a wild swing. He only manages to get an inside edge onto his pads though.
Tucks it around the corner for a run.
Steps down the track, Fakhar mistimes it to long on for a run.
Down the leg side, Zaman goes for the sweep but misses. Once again the umpire does not signal it as a wide.
Fires it on middle, Zaman pushes it to mid-wicket.
Dances down the track, takes it on the full and eases it down to long on to give Zaman the strike.
Shortens his length this time and bowls it on off, Zaman pushes it to covers.
FOUR! Cracked! This time Zaman does connect! Full and wide outside off, Zaman slaps it through covers and the ball races away. He is now 6 away from a half ton.
Wide outside off, the sucker ball. Zaman does go after it but does not connect.
On the pads, Zaman flicks it through backward square leg. Ngarava runs to his right from fine leg, dives and keeps it down to two. Good effort by the tall fast bowler.
Slower ball outside off, Zaman mistimes it to covers.
On the shorter side outside off, Zaman does not play a shot at it.
Uses his feet but does not get to the pitch of it. He drives it back to the bowler.
Fires it on off, Imam drives it back to the bowler.
Uses his feet this time and drives it down to long off for a run.
Deft! This time he paddle sweeps it through fine leg and takes two.
FOUR! Swept and swept hard! Goes down on one knee and with the turn, he sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Flighted ball on middle, Zaman drives it back to the bowler.
Three times in a row! Slightly short again outside off, Imam plays a nothing stroke. He tries to guide it down to third man but once again is beaten.
BEATEN AGAIN! This time it is the fuller delivery outside off, Imam lunges and tries to drive but does not connect.

Nicely bowled! A little zip off the surface for the bowler. Length ball outside off, this one skids through. Imam tries to guide it through the off side but gets beaten. Excitement in the crowd but nothing from the players.
Fuller on off, Zaman eases it down to long off for another single.
Slightly shorter in length on off, Imam whips it through mid-wicket for a run.
Just ahead of a length on off, Zaman pushes it to mid off.
Driven towards the mid off region. Good running between the wickets to pick up three runs. Pakistan are going at exactly 6 per over.
WIDE! Fires this down the leg side, Zaman misses the sweep. The keeper fails to collect it and the batsmen take two.
OOOOHHHH! Quicker and outside off, Zaman goes back and tries to cut. The ball is a little too close to play that shot. He gets beaten.
Flatter on off, Zaman punches it to covers.
Slightly short on middle, Imam goes back and flicks it to mid-wicket for a run.
Tosses this one up, Imam flicks it to mid-wicket.
Works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Now a maximum of 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over and they do need extra protection. Also, Tendai Chisoro is into the attack.
A dot to end Powerplay 1! Full and on off, Zaman strokes it to mid on. An excellent one for Pakistan, they are 59 for 0.

FOUR! A little uppish but in the gap! Full and on off, Zaman strokes it past the diving mid off for a boundary. He now is on 26, equal to Imam. He got off the mark when Imam was on 18. Has played the catch-up game really well.
On the pads, Zaman flicks it through square leg for a run.
WIDE! The bowler may have seen Zaman give him the charge. He goes for the wide yorker but bowls it a little too wide. The umpire stretches his hands.

FOUR! On the pads, a batsman of Zaman's caliber will not miss out. He flicks it fine down the leg side and the ball races away. 50 up for Pakistan. This is the third time in this series the openers have added more than 50.
Full again on off, FZ times it to mid off.

A huge appeal from the players and an extended one by the crowd but the umpire shakes his head. Tiripano pitches this one around leg, Zaman swings but misses. He gets hit on the pads. Pitched outside leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Slower ball down the leg side, Zaman tries to flick but misses. The ball brushes his pads and goes towards the keeper. He does well to dive to his right and stop it. Saves at least a couple there.
Outside off, Zaman goes after it with no foot movement. He gets beaten.
Shorter in length on middle, Imam rides over the bounce, rolls his wrists on top of it, keeps it along the ground towards fine leg and takes a run.
Fuller in length on off, Zaman drives it wide of mid off and takes a run. Good by him, got a boundary from the last ball and now takes a single.
FOUR! BOOM! Two tight overs and something had to give. Zaman brings out the heave, does not get it off the middle but connects well to clear the mid-wicket fielder and the ball crosses the boundary.
Yes, he does! Goes fuller again. Imam too drives it sweetly but finds mid off. Two tight overs in a row.
On a length again on off, Imam defends it solidly. Just a single from this over till now, can he finish it well?

This should cool him down now! Poor from Zimbabwe. Three dots and they should be looking to build the pressure and not give away an easy run. The fielders were at the edge of the circle. Keeping that in mind Zaman taps it towards covers and takes a quick run.
Three brilliant drives! On a fuller length on off, the batsman strokes it well but finds mid off. So three excellently timed strokes but no runs. A little frustrating for Zaman.
Full again on middle, Zaman once again times it back towards the bowler who makes a good stop in his followthrough.
Goes full on off, Zaman times it to the man at mid off.
A nice tight over by Blessing. Zimbabwe need a few more like these. Length and outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Make that 2 from the 5 balls. Down the leg side, Zaman clips it to fine leg for a run.
Fuller on off, it is eased to mid off. Just a run from the first 4 balls.
On a length and angling away from the batsman. Imam tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes down to third man for a run.
Good length on the stumps, Imam defends it to mid on.
On a length outside off, the batsman makes a leave.

Another excellent shot by Imam! Not a lot wrong with the delivery. It was on a length and around off, Imam goes back, uses his wrists and punches it through wide mid on. The fielder from mid on gives it a chase and saves a run for his side. 10 runs from Tiripano's first over and Pakistan are off to an excellent start.
First good ball by Tiripano in this over. On a length around off, Imam defends it towards point.
Shortish and width on offer outside off, Imam misses out there as he goes for a cut but misses.
He is bowling a touch too straight. Imam flicks it through mid-wicket and runs two.
Another short ball, this time though he gets away with it as Zaman mistimes his pull towards fine leg for a run.

FOUR! Welcome into the attack, Tiripano! A nothing ball to begin with. Short and on the pads. Zaman says thank you very much as he picks it up over the square leg fielder for a boundary. Can't bowl such balls to a batsman who is in immense form.
Donald Tiripano is into the attack.
This time Zaman takes a single on the last ball! On a length around off, he strokes it towards mid off for a quick run.
Zaman clips it towards Chisoro at mid-wicket and thinks about a run. The fielder runs to his left, dives and stops it. Seeing the effort the batsmen opt against it.
Fuller in length on middle, Zaman srokes it to mid on.
A little too straight by Muzarabani. Imam clips it through the leg side and takes a run.
Hits the length around off, Imam shuffles across and defends it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Good finish for Zimbabwe to an expensive over. 10 from it. Ngarava lands it on a length around off, kept out.
And he is off the mark straightaway. Short and wide outside off, Fakhar feeds on such deliveries. He cuts it through cover-point and runs another double.
Down the leg side again, Imam flicks it down to fine leg and he FINALLY, gives the strike over to Zaman.
FOUR! Imam is on a roll here! This is on the shorter side. He picks the length up early and pulls it through mid-wicket. The ball races to the fence. His second boundary in the 17 he has scored.
Clips it with the angle to the man at mid-wicket.
WIDE! Sprays in line and bowls it down the leg side. The umpire signals it as a wide.
A brace! Once again Imam is offered a little room outside off, he likes that. He punches it through cover-point and takes two.

Another single on the last ball! So Imam has faced all the 18 balls till now and he will be facing the 19th as well. This is on the fuller side. Imam flicks it through mid-wicket and takes a run. A good over by Blessing comes to an end, just a single off it.
Fuller in length on middle, Imam eases it to mid on.
Hits the length hard, it is defended. Good second over till now by Muzarabani.
Good length on off, the batsman defends it stoutly.
Length ball outside off, Imam makes a leave.
A good short ball but Imam does well to get on top of the bounce and pull it to mid-wicket.
Once again a single to finish the over. So Zaman has to wait to face his first ball. On a length around middle, Imam works it through square leg with the angle and takes a run.
Three good balls in a row! So this has been a good comeback after going for a boundary on the first ball. On a length and around off, Imam is solid in defense.
Back of a length on off, Imam goes back and keeps it out. Two good balls in a row. This is what he should continuously bowl.
Attacks the line on off, Imam defends it onto the ground.
On the pads this time, Imam works it around the corner and runs two.

FOUR! Not the start Ngarava would have wanted but full marks to Imam! Top shot by him! Slightly short and outside off, not too much width on offer but the amount offered was enough for him. He rocks back and punches it through covers, the timing is such that the ball races away to the fence. First boundary for him.
Richard Ngarava to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
A single to end the first over! A good one for the visitors. Down the leg side, tucked around the corner and Imam will retain strike for the next over.
A little wide outside off, the batsman need not play at it.

FOUR LEG BYES! Another beauty! Full marks to the bowler but it has cost him runs. He lands it on a length around middle, this one pitches and straightens. Imam tries to defend but does not account for the away movement. The ball brushes his pads and then goes towards first slip where Hamilton Masakadza fails to stop it and the ball races to the third man fence.
Almost! A poor delivery but almost provides a wicket. Short and very wide outside off, Imam throws the kitchen sink at it but misses. The umpire signals it as a wide.
Better from Muzarabani! On a length and around off, Imam gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it onto the ground.
Once again on the pads, Imam flicks it through square leg, past the diving fielder for a brace. Pakistan and Imam are underway.
A false start, down the leg side, Imam seems to have missed the flick but strangely the umpire does not signal it a wide. It may have flicked the trouser on the way.

We are all set to begin. The Pakistan openers, Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq make their way out to the middle. Blessing Muzarabani will start the proceedings from the City End, this is the first time he will be bowling from that end in the series. Can he price out an early wicket? We will find out as he comes running in to bowl the first ball.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo says the pitch looks an absolute belter. Further adds there is a little grass on it but it won't make a difference. Ends by saying these are wonderful batting conditions and runs are on offer.

Hamilton Masakadza says they are hoping for a win in the last two games. Adds further that should be very good for the boys. He feels the boys started well with the ball in the last game and he hopes they can nip out a couple of wickets early.

Sarfraz Ahmed says it looks like a good wicket. Adds further the sun is out and it should be good for batting. Ends by saying he is targeting a big total and hopes their batsmen get good batting practice.

TEAM CHANGES - Pakistan are playing the same team, whereas, Zimbabwe have made two changes. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, who is making his debut and Donald Tiripano come in for Prince Masvaure and Chamu Chibhabha.
TOSS - Pakistan win the toss and they will be batting first.

For Zimbabwe, it can't get any worse from the last game, right? One would surely say so, but looking at the series, their performance has been on a downward spiral. Let us hope they turn up today and show some fight. Stay tuned for further updates.

The sorry tour for the hosts continues as we welcome you to game 4 between Zimbabwe and Pakistan at Queens Sports Club, Bulawayo. It is a dead rubber as Pakistan have already sealed the series. However, they would want to win this one as well as they will be looking for a whitewash. Complacency is something Sarfraz will not appreciate in this game and he would hope his side would give it its all. With the series already in the bag, we might see them tinker with their eleven.
